target_customer: US military installations, federal agencies, state and local law enforcement, stadiums and critical infrastructure operators that need to detect hostile or unauthorized drones
problem: Cheap commercial drones can surveil or attack sensitive sites, while existing counter-drone detection is expensive and bulky. Detection has to cost about as little as the threat.
business_model: Hardware sensors plus software subscription and government contracts (AFWERX SBIR)
product_category: Passive RF drone detection and pilot geolocation (counter-UAS)

founders.name: Lucas Raskin
founders.background_notes: Before the hackathon he expected a career in telecommunications; later worked with Ukrainian ground troops gathering drone behavior data (Space Capital article).

founders.name: John Andrzejewski
education: Georgetown University, physics major, class of 2025
founders.background_notes: Expected a finance career before the hackathon.

founders.name: Eli Kerstein
education: Georgetown University, physics major, class of 2024
founders.background_notes: Background in physics and computer science per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Signal processing to detect and classify drone control links and geolocate pilots passively, plus a hardware prototype built in days. Needs RF hardware, embedded work and field validation, harder than software only.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary signal processing and government past performance (AFWERX SBIR, DIU challenge win) help, but passive RF detection is an established category with many vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established counter-UAS vendors already sold RF detection. No sign any copied or bought Guardian RF as of the latest sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Founders cite the DoD Joint Counter-small UAS Office, homeland drone incidents and Ukraine drone warfare. Demand for cheap detection grew through 2024 and 2025 (company long description and Georgetown article).

branding.name_origin: Founder Lucas Raskin said Guardian reflects protecting people and doing what is right, and a proactive stance on drone threats. The team first called itself Georgetown Physics at the hackathon.
branding.domain_note: guardianrf.com, an RF suffix on the word Guardian; no purchase story found

identity.logo: Grey symbol mark on the site

branding.community_and_virality: Press about the team rather than the brand: Georgetown features and Forbes 30 Under 30 2026 listing for the founders.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic defense name with no mascot or community; credibility comes from contracts and the founders story, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Guardian RF is active and still early. The team won attention by building a hardware prototype in days after a defense hackathon, then landed an AFWERX Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR at Vandenberg, a DIU low-cost sensing challenge win at Falcon Peak 25.2 and a February 2026 partnership with Picogrid. Funding is reported only by aggregators, so capital strength is unverified. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news was found.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators report a seed of about 2.0 to 2.5M USD (VCBacked 2.5M in 2024-09, Yespress about 2.3M in 2025-05, CB Insights 2M, PitchBook 625K) with General Catalyst, Space Capital and YC; no press release or company post confirmed an amount, so no round is recorded. Space Capital confirms a portfolio relationship only. Competition list left empty because the searches returned only 2025 and 2026 sources, none dated near the S24 batch. Ukraine sale claim is from a single profile and unverified.
